- Dungeon Monster Master

This game features exhilarating combat where you build up power through defense and unleash devastating attacks, combined with horror elements in which the monsters you love turn against the protagonist.

■ Game Features

  • Thrilling combat where you accumulate power through defense and unleash powerful attacks

  • A horror storyline where someone you love transforms into a monster and attacks you

  • An unpredictable story full of twists and surprises

■ Demo Story
HERO and his beloved MIKO have defeated the Demon King MEPITOS and restored peace to the world. However, MEPITOS's final attack transforms MIKO into a terrifying monster.

As monsters bearing MIKO's appearance begin attacking one after another, HERO finds himself unable to bring himself to defeat her. Even more strangely, among these monsters is one MIKO who tries to protect HERO.

Perhaps MIKO's soul still remains within her. Hoping to find a way to restore her to her original form, HERO sets out on a journey to find a wise sage who knows the magic that can save her.

After a long journey, the hero and his companions finally reach the dungeon of the final Demon Lord.

When the battle ends, they make an important promise to each other.

But peace never returns after the battle.

Instead, what awaits them is the sight of her, changed beyond recognition.

A mind-blowing horror-action boss rush RPG!

The monster he loves most, the Shrine Maiden, now seeks to kill him.

The hero, whom she simply cannot bring herself to kill with her own hands.

And an unknown monster that seeks the hero's death.

Their terrifying adventure begins...

Worldwide language support!

Easy Controls!(pad compatible)

Charge up your Power Slash by guarding, then unleash an overwhelmingly powerful slash with the attack button!

Experience thrilling combat and the satisfaction of landing devastating blows!

An ultimate action RPG set in an infinite open-world where you collect monsters, farm, and build your own world!

Become the protagonist of a mysterious world, tame and grow over 200 cute monsters, and build your own home.

Craft your own tools and face powerful boss monsters waiting for you.

Your grown monsters will protect you.

Enjoy thrilling boss battles in boss rush mode.

Explore a randomly changing, procedurally generated open world.

- Boss Dungeon with Powerful Bosses Waiting

You become the protagonist of a mysterious monster world and must find dungeons containing boss monsters to challenge them and save the world.

Collect and train monsters to fight boss monsters, defeat them, and obtain dungeon badges.

Collect all badges to challenge the final boss.

Combo attacks, dodging, and thrilling boss battles await you.

- An RPG Where You Challenge Dungeons with Your Companions

You are the leader of this adventure. Join forces with your companions and defeat powerful bosses.

Collect gold, purchase and upgrade equipment in town, and grow your companions as you explore dangerous dungeons.

Complete quests in town and save the world!

- Monster Collection and Training

Over 200 different monsters inhabit this mysterious world.

You can collect and tame these monsters.

Each monster has different abilities and growth rates.

Build your ultimate monster party of companions.

Well-trained monsters evolve into even stronger forms through evolution.

Collect special eggs found throughout the world and raise the monsters that hatch from them.

Build monster farms and raise them there.

Collect all monsters in the world and complete your monster encyclopedia collection.

- Various Attributes and Skills

There are many different attributes in this mysterious monster world:

Pickaxe, sword, fire, water, grass, electricity, angel, demon, darkness, light...

Various skills and magic also contain different attributes.

Understand and utilize attribute interactions to defeat your enemies.

In boss rush battles, your understanding of skills and magic will truly shine.

- Build Your Own City

Using the crafting techniques you learn, you can build and manage your own city.

First, clear the surrounding area to establish your city.

Then build the city you envision.

If you want to improve the environment, construct air purification buildings.

If you want to strengthen monster training, build monster farms.

To secure resources, build factories to increase city money.

- Infinite Random Open World

Enjoy exploration in an endlessly expanding, randomly generated world.

Experience changing terrain, monsters, and events every time you play.

Your experience will sometimes help you, and other times surprise you with completely new situations.

Demo Controls

  • Arrow Keys: Move

  • Z, X, C, V, A, S, D, F: Attack & Use Skills

  • B, N, R, Q, W, E, R: Demo Version Special Skills

  • T: Tame Monster Skill

  • Shift: Dodge

  • Number Keys (1–0): Use Inventory Slots

  • Esc: Game Menu

  • Mouse: Control Monsters & Use the Inventory

Heroes clock out. Cleanup clocks in.


The raid is over, the treasure room is empty, and somebody has to put the dungeon back together.

Dungeon Overtime is a compact desktop-idle management game about running the night shift between heroic invasions. Click to clear the first messes yourself, hire a strange cleanup crew, and build an increasingly fast automation machine that gets the dungeon ready for its next profitable disaster.

Clean up the chaos


Every raid leaves real work behind. Collect dropped loot, repair traps, restock treasure, rebuild bridges, and prepare each room for the next group of adventurers. Help directly by clicking or let your crew take over while you focus on the bigger picture.

Build your night shift


Unlock slimes, skeletons, mimics, and other helpers. Assign them to rooms, move them whenever priorities change, and level them up to multiply both manual work and automation.

Turn work into a machine


Upgrade every room, improve its automation, and invest in a global skill tree. New perks change how the whole dungeon operates—from stronger raid fighters and better clicks to faster cleanup and more valuable loot.

Make every raid count


Choose how deep the next raid should go. More active rooms mean stronger enemies, longer cleanup, and much larger rewards. Fight alongside your raider with well-timed clicks, hunt wandering loot goblins, and save rare potions for a boosted run.

Made for your desktop


Dungeon Overtime can live in a compact window while you work, study, or watch something else. Start actively, automate gradually, and check in whenever you feel like optimizing the next step.

  • Eight handcrafted dungeon rooms with distinct jobs and rewards
  • Manual clicking that grows into rapid automation
  • Movable cleanup workers with unique multipliers and upgrades
  • Room levels, enemy scaling, raid combat, and boss encounters
  • A global, draggable skill tree with branching upgrades
  • Random loot goblins and potions that reward active play
  • Optional auto-raids and unlockable speed controls
  • A compact pixel-art interface designed for desktop play

Dungeon Picnic is a party-building roguelike RPG that distills everything great about RPGs into one package.

Even a single short run delivers the full thrill of an RPG.

Combine randomly appearing skills and equipment to build your own ultimate party and take down powerful enemies.

Party Building, Not Deck Building

Combine allies and equipment to unlock explosive combos.

Enjoy building your entire party as one.

Break the Limits, Turn Them Into Power

Skills have cooldowns, and the more powerful the move, the more carefully you need to manage it - but cooldowns aren't just a restriction.

Turn restrictions into strengths - like an ultimate move that costs every other skill's cooldown, or a skill that ignores cooldowns entirely.

Use all kinds of broken skills and break the limits.

Fast-Paced Turn-Based Battles Where Teamwork Is Key

There's no individual MP per character - instead, like a card game, your whole party shares a single "Mana" pool.

Break an enemy and you'll get an extra turn, increased mana recovery, and reduced mana costs.

Attack an enemy while it's broken and your critical hit rate goes up too.

Do you go all-in with a high-cost skill, or deliberately break the enemy with a support character to feed mana to your party?

Take control of your resources with flexible, on-the-fly strategy.

Also, mastering your allies' combo skills lets you unleash follow-up attacks and counters that ignore turn order entirely.

Roguelike game

When a party is defeated, you lose all your skills and equipment.

But since the skills and gear you find are randomized each time, you can enjoy the fun of creating a new party build every run.

Steal the Dream. Survive the Wake.


Every night, Sookuma descends into a dungeon that rearranges itself beneath the dream. Every step is a turn. Every sound can draw something closer. Somewhere below, the Dream Crystal is waiting.

Reach it, steal it, and the entire dungeon wakes up.

Then comes the hard part: climbing all the way back to the silver stairs on the first floor—alive.

Build a Sookuma That Changes the Run


Choose one of 14 Sookuma lineages and pair it with one of 19 classes. A lineage changes the body you bring into the dream; a class changes how you survive it. Combine passive traits, lineage powers, class abilities, starting equipment, and learned skills into a build of your own.

  • 14 lineages with distinct passives, active powers, silhouettes, colors, ears, fur, and clothing
  • 19 classes spanning melee fighters, hunters, scholars, alchemists, assassins, summoners, and stranger callings
  • 21 use-based skills across three groups—Basics, Weapons, and Spells—that improve as you rely on them
  • Eight-directional combat shaped by accuracy, evasion, armor, resistances, positioning, and status effects



Nothing Is What It Seems


Potions, scrolls, and wands do not politely explain themselves. Their appearances are reshuffled between dreams, so knowledge must be earned by experimenting, reading, and surviving the consequences.

  • 137 items, including 74 pieces of equipment with individual enchantments, brands, curses, and equipment comparisons
  • 42 spells, including 10 summoning spells, powered by mana
  • Unknown consumables that reveal their true identity only through discovery and use
  • Auto-explore, automatic pickup, targeting previews, contextual logs, shops, and NPC encounters keep the focus on decisions

Listen to the Gods—or Defy Them


Nineteen gods wait at their altars, each with a voice, a temperament, and powers they are willing to grant. Hear a god describe its covenant before you decide. Earn piety, invoke divine abilities, abandon your patron for another—or refuse them all. Betrayal is remembered, and divine wrath can outlive devotion.



A Dungeon That Hears You


Vision ends at the edge of the torchlight, but danger does not. Noise travels through corridors. Traps hide beneath familiar floors. Monsters hunt in packs, and named enemies announce that the dream has taken a personal interest in you.

  • A 15-floor main dungeon, six side branches, and two portal dungeons: the Dream Sewers, which stays open, and the Dream Bazaar, which closes after one visit
  • Six procedural layout families mixing rooms, tunnels, caverns, hives, and fractured sanctums
  • 193 enemies: 150 monster species, 35 named foes, and 8 area bosses, with packs and threats capable of pursuing you between floors
  • Limited sight, exploration fog, sound propagation, hidden traps, and persistent floor state

Going Down Is Only Half the Journey


The deepest floor is not the finish line. Taking the Dream Crystal changes the rules and turns every floor you survived into an escape route. Spend what remains. Choose what to leave behind. Find the path you opened on the way down—and fight back through it before the dream closes around you.

Three endings await, shaped by the Crystal and by how completely you conquered the dungeon.

Death ends this dream. The next one will open again.

Welcome to Dungeon Town Life – your very own adventure!

Your life as an adventurer begins in a remote, peaceful village where a mysterious portal has recently appeared. Join the local Adventurers' Guild, forge your own legends and shape your life exactly the way you want – whether in the deepest dungeons or in cozy village life.

Join the Adventurers' Guild

Head to the village notice board, accept quests and climb the ranks of the guild. Together with your friends, fight your way through dangerous procedural dungeons, defeat mighty bosses, collect valuable loot and level up your character step by step.

Forge, Plant & Build

A true adventurer relies on their own skills!

  •  Forge your own weapons: Collect rare ores from the depths of the dungeons and craft your own gear at the village forge.

  • Grow healing herbs: Create your own garden bed, sow useful plants and brew powerful potions for your next raids.

  •  Your own home: Expand your house to your liking and create a refuge to rest after hard battles.

A living world with a day and night cycle

Experience a dynamic world that follows a natural daily rhythm. Use the daylight to step through the portal, explore dungeons and gather valuable resources. Once night falls, the portal gates close – the perfect time to return to the village, process your loot, brew potions, expand your home or prepare for the next day.

Stronger together – co-op multiplayer

You don't have to face the dangers alone! Team up with your friends to explore dungeons together, share the loot and watch each other's backs in tight fights.

Get ready to step through the portal. Your adventure, your dungeon, your loot!

■ Live in the labyrinth. The way you play becomes your skills.

Skills here aren't picked from a list.

The game keeps track of what you do in the labyrinth,

and only players who keep at something reach the skill that matches it.

More than 40 skills. What awakens them is for you to find out.

■ See it. Choose. Make it in time.

Enemy attacks telegraph before they land.

Watch, then guard, parry or dodge.

Parry cleanly and the enemy staggers, opening a window to strike back.

This isn't about trading blows behind flashy effects. It's built around the feel of seeing, choosing and making it in time. Wield a sword or a greatsword.

■ Catch monsters and dive together

Weaken a monster and catch it with a Capture Card.

Your companions come into the dungeon with you and fight at your side.

Each has its own talent, like sniffing out treasure, to help you through the labyrinth.

■ Send your companions into the arena

Build a team from the monsters you've raised and send them into battle in the arena.

■ A labyrinth that changes every run

Terrain, enemy placement and what's inside the chests change every time.

Meadow, volcano and snowfield each hold their own dangers.

Dive into the same labyrinth with up to three friends.

■ The master of the 10th floor

A master waits on the 10th floor. Parry it, break its stance, and bring it down.

Take what it leaves behind to the blacksmith in town and forge new weapons and armor.

■ Fall, and come back for it

If you fall, what you picked up stays on that floor.

Reach it again and recover your share.

■ Gear up in town, then dive again

Stock up at the item shop and upgrade your gear at the blacksmith.

Change your look anytime at the inn's mirror.

■ Up to 4 players via Steam friends

Invite friends straight from your Steam friends list and dive in together.

Solo works too.

■ Built in Early Access

I'll keep adding monster types, environments, effects, dungeon hazards, player equipment and skills while listening to the people playing.

How far along the game is right now is laid out honestly in the "Early Access" section on this page.

Time is the only resource that matters

There is no health bar. There is a clock, and it is always running.

Every hit you take is seconds gone. Every wrong step, every trap, every enemy that reaches you first costs time you cannot get back. When the clock hits zero, the run is over. The only way to survive is to keep moving down.

Find the exit. Decide what is worth the detour. Get out before the timer

decides for you.

Get stronger, then lose it all

Every floor you clear offers a choice. Build a run that works, push deeper than

last time, and start over when it ends.

Find out what happened to them

The dungeon has people in it. Talk to them, look for what they left behind,

and reach an ending that fits what you found.

Features

Time as health — one resource for fighting, exploring and risking

Hand-built floors, each with its own threat

Turn-based combat on a grid

Permanent progression between runs

DungeonBox is a party RPG for up to 8 players. Everyone plays from their own phone: submit your funniest ideas, vote for the best one, and watch the story bend around whatever your party decides.

Your Dungeon Master (run by your choice of a player or computer DM) sets the scene and everyone answers at once: heroic, clever or completely unhinged. Players join from their phone's browser with a room code. No app, no account, no extra controllers.

Every answer lands on the big screen. The party votes, the best idea scores, and the winning move becomes the story, consequences and all.

Pick a lock, spot a trap, slap a gnome. Risky moves call for a skill check rolled right from your phone, and your class, stats and items tip the odds. A natural 20 is legendary. So is a natural 1.

Descend into the Lion's Labyrinth, a papercraft dungeon crawl where every player steers their own hero. Search chests, sniff out hidden keys, outwit trolls and mimics, and fight turn-based battles on the way to the Gilded Serpent's hoard.

When a quest turns violent, the whole party votes on cards: back your heroes' attacks and block the enemy's nastiest moves. Loot a million gold, survive a Super Blast, or simply stand there looking cool.

  • Up to 8 players, one phone each – join with a room code, or fill empty seats with CPU players.

  • A Dungeon Master who never runs out of ideas – every answer changes the story, narrated aloud.

  • Draw it into existence – sketch magic items and monsters on your phone and watch them come to life in the dungeon.

  • Build your character – choose from 12 heroes, earn XP, raise your stats and unlock abilities like Fireball, Pickpocket and Diss Track.

  • Hand-written quests, endless outcomes – from tavern brawls to pirate-ship escapes, with 100 random events waiting to shake things up.

  • Your table, your rules – set the Content Rating anywhere from “Family Friendly” to “Anything Goes”.

  • Made for streaming – extra viewers join as the audience and vote, and the room code can be hidden on stream. Remote Play Together supported.

  • 12 languages – menus, quests and narration fully localized.

Dungeoneers Idle is an endless idle RPG about building a party and letting it work, with the option to jump in and play any hero yourself.

Assemble a team from twelve hero classes, carve each hero's path through a huge passive tree, and send them into procedurally generated dungeons. Combat resolves itself. Your job is the decisions that matter: who goes, which skills they bring, what they wear and which piece of gear is worth crafting into something special. Early on you make those calls by hand. Later, you buy the automation that makes them for you.

It keeps going when you don't. Close the game, come back tomorrow, and your party will have spent the night clearing dungeons, levelling up and swapping in better gear.

It doesn't run out. Hero levels have no cap, the depths keep scaling as fast as your party does, and every prestige measures you against your own deepest run rather than a fixed target. This is an idler built for months, not for an evening.

Keep it on your desktop

Companion Mode folds the game into a small, see-through window you can place anywhere on your screen. Your party keeps fighting while you work, watch something or play another game, and a double-click brings the full game back.

Build a party, then let it work

  • Twelve hero classes: Warrior, Mage, Rogue, Cleric, Ranger, Pyromancer, Druid, Necromancer, Barbarian, Ninja, Electromancer and Bard. Five are yours from the start.

  • Hand-authored skills, unlocked and levelled with gold. Each hero carries only two (at first) into a dungeon, so a loadout is a real decision rather than a checklist.

  • A passive tree of over 1000 nodes for every hero. Save your favourite builds or export them as a code to share, and two heroes of the same class can still play nothing alike.

  • Start with room for two heroes and earn your way to four.

Dungeons that build themselves

  • Five dungeon types: Crypt, Cave, Fortress, Temple and Frost. Generated fresh every time, each with its own themed enemies.

  • An overworld of eight biomes to push outward through, from plains and forest to volcanic wastes.

  • Combat with status effects, elites, bosses and summoned minions.

  • Enemies, bosses and dungeon art made from scratch for this game, from scrappy goblin raiders to a Goblin King in a crown he definitely stole.

See it through their eyes

  • Hero View: watch any dungeon in first person, through the eyes of one of your heroes.

  • Take Over: grab the controls and play that hero yourself, with WASD and the mouse, while the rest of the party fights alongside you. Hand them back whenever you like.

  • Arrows and spells fly for real and light up the dark as they go. Knock the dead flying with ragdoll corpses.

  • Nine extra achievements and three trials just for steering a hero. All optional, so idle players miss nothing.

Gear worth chasing

  • Five rarities, Common through Legendary. Epic and Legendary pieces roll three or four stats, so no two drops look alike.

  • 80 special effects that change how a hero fights, many made for a single class: crits that freeze enemies solid, a basic attack that strikes twice, enemies that explode when they die, an angel that pulls a hero back from death once per dungeon.

  • Effects roll their own strength, so there is always a better version out there.

  • Lock your favourites so nothing great ever gets sold by accident.

Make your best gear even better

Found something you love? Keep it. Crafting turns the gear you would have thrown away into the gear you never take off.

  • Salvage what you don't need into Shards.

  • Hone a single stat a little higher with every try.

  • Reforge an old favourite up to your current depth, so a great find stays great.

  • The toughest monsters leave rare trophies behind that give your best pieces an extra line.

  • Bank the best stats and effects from every Epic and Legendary you salvage, then imprint them onto the gear you actually wear.

Automate yourself out of a job

The dungeoneering runs itself from the first minute. Your party explores, fights and hauls loot home whether you are watching or not.

The managing doesn't, though. Not at first. Early on you level your heroes by hand, spend their passive points, pick their gear and decide what's worth keeping. Then you start buying that work away. Auto-level, Auto-Delve through the passive tree, auto skill levelling, Auto-Equip, loot filters, Auto-Hone: every one of them is a job you do for the last time.

Progress that carries over

  • Gold replaces experience. Everything the party earns is also everything you spend.

  • Prestige when the depth stops giving, and convert the run into permanent progress.

  • A branching meta tree with a branch for every class, plus automation, economy, alchemy, crafting, party size and more.

  • Nine potions to unlock, collect and use.

Challenges and achievements

  • 25 challenges that bend the rules of a run, from melee-only parties to monsters that never stop healing.

  • Every challenge has five medals, Bronze to Diamond, and each one gives that save a permanent bonus.

  • 100 achievements, each with a small permanent bonus for all your saves.

Idle on your terms

  • Buy it once. No microtransactions and no premium currency.

  • Offline progress. The simulation catches up on the time you were away, and if you’re in a hurry, you can skip the wait and take the gold.

  • Playable with the mouse alone. Taking over a hero is entirely optional, so nothing ever asks for quick reflexes.

  • Three named save slots.

  • Optional keyboard shortcuts for opening menus, if you'd rather not reach for the mouse.

  • Steam Cloud support, so your saves and builds follow you to every PC.

Dungeoneers Idle asks for a few minutes of decisions and gives you back the rest of the day.

Football Manager, but every match is a dungeon and your players can die in it.

You run an adventuring guild in a realm that lost its king. Sign delvers, swear them to a term of years and send them into the dark. Win enough and you take the Crucible, and hold the realm until somebody takes it off you.

Heroes die. Dynasties rise. The realm remembers both.

Every fixture is a dungeon

There is no match engine. Each delve is built for the day, and in the Trials a rival guild goes into the same one. If they make it to the final room, you fight them there.

You never click an attack. You pick the party, set their orders and kit them out, then you watch. Flooded ground slows your fighters and pitch dark ruins your archers, so who you send matters as much as how strong they are. Nine classes, ten races, and a party that grows from four to six as you climb six divisions.

People, not numbers

Every delver arrives believing something, struggling with something, and swearing to do one thing before they are done. Most never manage it. Sending the right one on the right work, year after year, is how you find out who they are.

They make friends and grudges underground. They sign for a term of years and come back asking for what they are worth. They pick up scars, retire, get sold, or do not come home, and the dead get a memorial card with their own sigil and epitaph. The Dungeonborn are the ones that you bring back.

A realm that goes on without you

Seventy-two guilds hold seats in 36 towns across seven lands, so you share a street with somebody who wanted to better you before a fixture was ever played. Rival halls sign, sell, rise and fall. Wars are called and the realm remembers who marched. Beasts roam the roads, and below everything the Deep goes down further than anyone has been.

Your own hall stands in a real town that you can build up, defend, and one day watch your retired delvers settle in.

The Chronicle

Your guild has been writing it down the whole time. Open the Chronicle and the dynasty is there as a story, season by season, with the fallen and the legends who made the place what it is. Everything in it happened in your save.

Play it your way

Climb from the Backwater or start higher up. Take a patron's backing or go it alone. Stack any of the founding terms you like, from Ironman to a guild made entirely of beasts, or play Cozy Mode with no league at all and simply run the guild.

  • 72 rival guilds, six divisions, a cup and the Crucible

  • A full transfer market, with free transfers, loans, poaching and fire sales

  • Training, a youth academy and mentors

  • Your hometown to build up and defend

  • Vows, families, scars and permanent death

  • Over a dozen founding terms that all stack, and Cozy Mode

  • Twelve languages besides English

The dungeon is waiting, Guildmaster.

One Character. Two Players. One Victory.

DuoControl is a unique online co-op PvP FPS where two players control a single character together. One player controls movement (Keyboard), while the other handles aiming and shooting (Mouse). Your opponents play by the same rules. Winning isn't just about having great aim—it's about perfect communication, coordination, and teamwork.

◆ How to Play

🎮 The Mover controls the character, takes positions, and leads the team's movement.

🎯 The Shooter aims, fires, and manages every engagement.

🤝 You share control of the same character, making every decision together.

⚡ Every match pits your duo against other teams using the same unique control system.

◆ Key Features

👥 Two Players, One Character
Experience a truly unique FPS mechanic where two players share control of a single soldier.

⚔️ 2v2 & 4v4 PvP Battles
Team up with a friend and compete against other coordinated duos.

🌐 Online Multiplayer
Invite a friend, choose your roles, and jump straight into the action.

🎯 Coordination-Driven Gameplay
Movement and aiming are controlled by different players, making teamwork the key to victory.

🔧 Customizable Crosshair
Each player can use their own preferred crosshair settings.

🚀 Fast-Paced Competitive Matches
Every game tests your reflexes, communication, and coordination.

◆ Who Is It For?

Perfect for players who enjoy cooperative gameplay, competitive PvP, and fresh FPS mechanics that reward teamwork over individual skill.

One player moves. One player shoots. Together, you control one soldier.

Your opponents do the same.

Victory belongs to the most coordinated team.

DuskLand: Poker Roguelike RPG with Spatial Strategy

Welcome to 《DuskLand》, a world consumed by dark chaos.

Form your party with heroes wielding unique abilities and stand against the surging chaotic beasts and formidable bosses!

🃏 Poker Hand-Based Strategic Combat

  • From One Pair to Flush and Straight! Complete familiar poker hands to unleash devastating damage combos.

  • Utilize dual counter system between elements and card suits to turn the tide of battle in critical moments.

🧩 Tetris-Style Grid Inventory System

  • Strategically position weapons and equipment within a limited inventory space.

  • Maximize adjacent synergies between cards and gear to create your own unique build.

⚔️ Diverse Party Combinations & Roguelite Growth

  • Assemble and refine your party with distinct characters, each possessing unique elements and domains.

  • Experience fresh strategic choices with every run through dynamic shops, card enhancements, and random events.

🏆 Chapter Rankings & Damage Competition

  • Prove your strategy as your highest damage achieved and deck composition for each chapter are recorded on the rankings.

  • Break through your limits with your own unique deck combinations, set new record scores, and compete for top ranks with players around the world.

Dusky's Nook is a cozy idle desktop game about a little mushroom guy living his life on a floating island.

Gather mushrooms
Dusky spends his days foraging on his own. Rare glowing mushrooms appear now and then — those ones only you can collect, for a big EXP boost.

Make the island yours
Level up to unlock new looks for Dusky and his island, light phases, the palette, the music, a few extra animations, and maybe even some new companions..

Three Phases of the day
Dawn, dusk, and night — each with its own light, mist, and drifting fireflies

Co-working companion
Put the island anywhere on your screen and resize it to fit. No timers, no notifications. A little to do if you want it, nothing asked of you if you don't. Dusky enjoys the company in any setting you want him!

Reach level 30 and new friends come to stay.

*Free content updates after launch*

Desert silence and a pickaxe in your hand. You head underground, and for a while the world above stops mattering.

Dust & Diamonds is a calm pixel-art game about digging, building and trading. You are a goblin with a handful of coins and a crumbling settlement at the edge of the desert. The rest you write yourself, one tile at a time.

Day and night over the desert

A day lasts half an hour: dawn, noon, a violet dusk, the moon over the rocks and lights in the windows. Sandstorms, vultures over the desert, caravans making camp in the distance. Sometimes a cat sleeps on the Shop roof. When it comes down, you can pet it.

A mine you'll want to come back to

Dig at your own pace. First dirt and coal, then gold, platinum, titanium and diamonds, all the way to the bottom, 100 metres below the surface. Place ladders, torches and support beams, pick up what you dig out, while your Workers carry goods from the chests back to the settlement. One more tunnel. Five more minutes.

The rock keeps its surprises

Behind the wall wait hidden pockets and caves, some with ore, some with water or lava. And water really flows. One swing of the pickaxe and the tunnel you dug so patiently has a river of its own.

The mountain likes to remind you it's there

No ceiling holds forever. You place your support beams with care, and when things start to crumble, you simply run. Then you come back with your pickaxe, one cave-in wiser.

A settlement that grows with you

Raise six buildings from the ruins: the Shop, Workshop, Warehouse, Greenhouse, Water Collector and Worker Hotel. Each has five levels and a rhythm of its own. The Workshop holds over 200 recipes, the Greenhouse its crops, and the Hotel Kitchen meals for your crew. Workers have names, skills and wages, and they'll let you know when they get hungry.

The Shop earns while you dig

Set your minimum prices, head underground, and the Shop keeps working. Customers come to the door, thirty of them by name, along with merchants and their own offers. Father has something to say about every one of them, in a voice of his own in every language of the game. The Business Chronicle remembers every product you've managed to sell.

Music to dig to

Dozens of music discs to collect. They play on the radio while you keep digging.

Play your way

Keyboard and mouse or gamepad. Three difficulty levels, a skippable tutorial, rebindable keys, colorblind mode, reduced effects and a larger interface. English, Polish, French, German, Spanish, Chinese and Russian.

Head down to the mine for a while. You'll see how quickly the evening goes.

Dwarf Hole is an incremental game about two things, Dwarves and Holes. Upgrade and guide your Dwarves to riches and turn them into the most optimized digging machines in the Hole.

Dig through the rock, uncover ores and most importantly make a bigger. deeper. hole. Every single pixel in the Hole is mineable and procedurally generated, who knows what's hiding under the stone?

Dwarves are your most important resource. Without them the hole doesn't get bigger or deeper. You would do well to keep them organized and playing to their strengths. Most Dwarves like it in the hole, and spend most of their time mining and climbing, just to fall and mine again.

Other Dwarves prefer to stay up top, and helping others achieve their deepest desires by directly lending a helping hand or are focused on achieving the newest advances in Dwarf technology.

Features:

  • Invest in 20+ upgrades

  • Unlock 60+ technologies

  • Equip your Dwarves with gear

  • Build out your mining camp

  • An original soundtrack

  • Localized in 14 languages

Dwarven Outpost: Incremental is the world's first 3D open-world survival cookie clicker — an incremental game you actually walk around in. You start in an empty clearing with one tuft of grass and a pair of hands. You leave with a dwarven outpost.

Mine, chop and gather across an open 3D world: rolling hills, hundreds of scattered trees and rocks, and fifty thousand tufts of grass — every single one of them harvestable. Whatever you take flies straight into your stockpile with a satisfying pull.

Automation & Offline Progress

Research auto-harvesting and your dwarf works the ground around him on his own, each resource at its own upgradeable pace. Walk, and the grass bursts open in your wake.

Log off and it keeps going. Production and survival run on the exact same tick offline as online, so you always come back to something new.

But automation only reaches so far. Once the area around you is picked clean, it's time to head out and find new ground. You are always the engine of progress.

Research & Build

Raise storage, a bed, a drying table and a fire pit. Turn raw forage into meals at the fire, keep your dwarf fed, rested and in good spirits — a happy dwarf works faster.

Twenty-eight research nodes across six tiers, drawn as a real graph with prerequisite lines. Research unlocks structure — whole tools, buildings and systems, so the interface grows with you. Repeatable upgrades handle the numbers. Work your way to the top of the tree and become Master of the Clearing.

  • Survival that nudges, never punishes. Food and sleep are soft pressure — a hungry dwarf is slower, not dead. There is no run to lose.

  • Mood matters. Your dwarf's spirits feed back into everything he does.

  • Mini Mode. Watch your dwarf auto harvesting while doing other work on the PC.

Strike the Wall

Your dwarf strikes the rock and showers the cavern floor with ore and gems. Grab them before they fade!

Level Up

With every piece of ore you collect, you gain experience. Each level-up lets you choose one of three cards that empowers your dwarf for the rest of the shift.

Stronger Every Shift

Spend your ore between shifts on a massive skill tree: critical strikes, mine carts, faster strikes, longer shifts and better luck.

Discover Powerful Relics

Powerful relics wait at the end of each mine. They let you ascend, grant unique bonuses and open new mines.

Dybbuk is a Single player / Hybrid PvP & Co-op horror game.

Teamwork Is Your Lifeline. Players must coordinate, communicate, and make difficult choices:

Should you split up to find statues faster?

Maybe it's better to stay together and fend off summoned creatures?

Do you risk carrying a statue alone?

Can you trust the player helping you, or is he already possessed?

Your decisions shape the flow of every match.

Face an ancient evil in this action multiplayer horror PvP/Co-op game.

A malevolent Dybbuk stalks your team. It is capable of summoning monsters, manipulating the environment utilizing supernatural abilities.

But the greatest threat is its hunger for a host.

When a player is caught by the Dybbuk, it becomes possessed and turns into the new demon with full control of its arsenal.

Gather your team, hunt the Dybbuk, and try to survive a shifting nightmare -

The monster can be any one of you!

Seal the Demon in the dybbuk box.

Your only hope is to locate and retrieve statues of Mesopotamian deities hidden throughout the environment. These sacred artifacts are the Dybbuk’s weakness. Return them to the Dybbuk Box, a vessel of containment and exorcism, to strip the demon of its powers.

  • Each statue removes one demonic ability

  • Every ability removed shifts the balance of power

  • The final statue will seal the Dybbuk in the box.

  • Carrying a statue makes you vulnerable.

The Dybbuk senses your intent and it will come for you.

A Win Condition Built on Urgency and Betrayal

Only non-possessed players can win. Once possessed, players must quickly pass the Dybbuk to another host before its abilities are stripped away! creating constant pressure and shifting power dynamics.

Key Features.

  • Levels are procedurally generated each match, delivering fresh layouts and unpredictable encounters for high replayability.

  • Face a highly adaptive and intelligent enemy AI that reacts to player behavior, tracks movement and sound, and dynamically adjusts its tactics. Enemies coordinate, ambush, and exploit mistakes creating tense, unscripted horror encounters.

  • PvP & Co-op Hybrid Gameplay Work together to survive, but prepare to face former teammates once they become possessed.

  • Dynamic Demon Abilities: The Dybbuk can summon creatures, set traps, deceive players, and more. Each deity statue removed strips the demon of one ability, creating shifting power waves throughout the match.

Command a squad against an army of the reanimated dead. Dynamic Breach is a top-down tactical shooter: lead your squad through Requiem, a campaign of 33 operations across 6 acts, solo or with up to three friends. Hold out in Onslaught, a horde mode with a boss every five waves. And take on other players in seven versus modes, online or on LAN, with a global Elo ranking.

REQUIEM - THE CAMPAIGN

33 operations, 6 acts, a hand-made map for each. Plus one hidden operation. Cutscenes, and several endings depending on the choices you make. Your squad follows your orders: move, focus a target, hold, follow. Play it solo with AI allies, or in co-op with up to three friends, online or on LAN.

THE DEAD

The dead you put down get back up, unless you burn them or finish them off. A Cantor raises them faster than you can cut them down, until you kill it. Choristers heal them, Wraiths jam your HUD, Bloaters burst into caustic rot. And the HERALD is a Cantor grown to a size that should not stand.

ONSLAUGHT - THE HORDE MODE

Mixed waves of mercenaries and the undead, and a HERALD boss every five waves. Solo with bots, or in co-op with up to three friends. Graded operation dossiers, browsable bestiary.

VERSUS - AGAINST OTHER PLAYERS

  • Breach - plant and defuse

  • Elimination

  • Team Deathmatch

  • Domination

  • Capture the Flag

  • Extraction - a package to carry out, position drawn at random

  • Blackout - free-for-all battle royale, 10 to 50 fighters, closing zone

Online through Steam, in a public lobby or by invitation, or on LAN: up to 10 players. Team modes are 5v5 and bots fill the empty slots, so two players are enough for a full match. Online, six modes count toward a global Elo ranking as soon as each side has a player. Nobody around? Every mode also plays offline against bots.

SEVEN CLASSES, SEVEN ABILITIES

  • Medic - healing aura (Rally)

  • Phantom - cloak

  • Shield - deployable barrier

  • Gunner - dig in

  • Assault - push

  • Engineer - proximity mine

  • Recon - recon drone

41 WEAPONS AND THE BLACK-TECH

41 weapons, from the issue sidearm to energy weapons, unlocked as you level up. And black-tech gear for whoever can afford it: force field, dampening weave, fission, plasma and singularity grenades.

PROGRESSION

A global level and grade, earned by playing, unlock the arsenal and cap upgrades. Upgrades are shared across the squad; levels belong to each operator individually.

ALSO

  • 39 Steam achievements and Steam Cloud saves

  • Fully in English and French: interface, campaign, in-game data

Dyneria simulates a fantasy world from the climate up. Rain falls where the winds carry it, rivers rise where the rain lands, forests follow the water, and eight races settle wherever the land can feed them.

  • The map is the simulation. Temperature and moisture move with the seasons and set everything under them. Rivers run where the rain lands, forests follow the rivers, deserts creep in where the rain stops coming. Farm the same ground hard enough for long enough and you can turn it into desert yourself.

  • Nothing is scripted and nothing spawns from a table. When two countries go to war or form an alliance, there's always a reason.

The Dwarves dig under the mountains and can't feed themselves. The Ravari nest in the canopy and hunt whoever lives under it. The Mirekin fish a coast until it's empty. Each race builds its own way.

  • Everyone wants something they can't make. The Dwarves want whiskey and the potatoes for it only grow in the cold corners. The Woodelves want mithril arrows and mithril seams are in short supply. So towns ask each other, and the usual answer is no. Getting refused is remembered, and it's how wars start.

  • A handful of iron sites on the whole map. Iron isn't in every hillside. A few places hold all of it, and the town that gets there first arms its soldiers better than its neighbours can. Countries try to please the towns that hold one, and when pleasing doesn't work, they may take it by force.

  • Wars with causes. Armies are raised from real villages and fed from real stores. Prey on weaker foe's, take away threats, fight for hungry mouths to feed. Or maybe, they have been deceived...

For better or for worse, you hold godly powers. As the years go on, your power grows. Take on aspects that shape your influence. 

  • Fire. Light a spark on dry ground and let the wind decide. Drop a meteor. Raise a volcano. Or ignite the fires of industry for an iron mine under a town you've decided to favour.

  • Nature. Rain, cold snaps, droughts, a locust swarm that wanders off wherever it likes. Grow forests and fertile lands. Create paradise, or take it away.

  • Religion. Build up a religion that superseeds country borders. Create believers all over the world, their believe gives you power, use or abuse, the choice is yours. 

  • Biology. Genes, mutations and virusses. Create a powerfull race, spread disease or conquer the world with a mutant army.

  • Politics. Install politicians who do your bidding. Shape allies or enemies, seed hatred trough propaganda, let villages owe you one, and cash in your chips when it's time to strike.

Play the game

Campaigns are adventures, a set world with a story to tell. An swamp invaded by mirekin, multiplying and aggressive. A lone Woodelf village, pushed back into their forest by a Ravari tribe. A world threatened by rumours of an orc invasion about to happen.

Core Gameplay: Automated production lines + Roguelike modifiers + Tower defense combat

Key Features: Runs on desktop, usable as desktop wallpaper, perfect for casual play at work

This is a desktop idle automation builder that blends roguelike modifiers and tower defense combat. Build automated production lines on your desktop, set up defenses, conduct research, stack tech modifiers, construct a Dyson Sphere, form a self-sustaining industrial system, and fend off alien invasions.

✅ 41 functional buildings covering harvesting, smelting, manufacturing, research and defense to run your full factory pipeline

✅ 34 raw materials and finished products, from basic ores to high-end tech goods, forming a complete closed-loop crafting system

✅ 28 unique modifiers — no flat stat boosts, with powerful synergies between them for creative builds

✅ 7 distinct defensive units: machine gun tower, missile tower, laser tower, drone command post and more, each with its own combat niche

✅ 30 research projects unlocking bonuses for production, logistics and combat to keep upgrading your factory

✅ Over 100 hours of gameplay, with varied builds for lasting strategic replay value

Place production buildings on your desktop and deploy drone logistics!

Launch units skyward to build stellar orbits!

Eliminate alien creatures and defend your units.！

Draw tech perks, forge your build, and skyrocket production efficiency!

A dead god drifts in the dark. Strip it to the bone.

Something colossal died out here a long time ago. You didn't kill it you're here to take it apart. Point a fleet of mining drones, turrets and collectors at the carcass and watch it come apart cell by cell: a procedurally-drawn pixel-art titan dissolving into a storm of flying salvage while the counters climb.

Every upgrade is something you SEE

This is a visual automation-incremental in the spirit of The Gnorp Apologue. You don't buy an abstract "+10% damage"  you bolt another turret onto the rig, watch a new drone peel off the hull, and see the carcass start disappearing faster.

Build a whole arsenal of crews, each stripping the carcass a different way: auto-lasers, demolition rockets, reeling harpoons, orbiting Tesla coils that arc lightning between each other, flamethrowers, charging railguns and more.

Make the weapons feed each other

The fun isn't in one weapon it's in the reactions. Freeze cells with Cryo so they stop drifting away and the rest of your fleet keeps landing clean hits. Drop Burn onto that frost for a chain explosion. Paint Acid patches that don't hurt on their own but amplify every other weapon firing inside them.

Sometimes the dead ones aren't dead

When a corpse runs dry, you go hunting for the next and the next specimen is alive. Drop the automation, take the stick, and duel it yourself in a real-time bullet-dance: dash through its attacks, tear off enough of it to crack the core open, and drag the fresh, bigger carcass home to strip. No two of them move the same.

Evolve, and go again on something bigger

Every expedition banks Genome you spend on a mutation loadout that reshapes the next run. Grow your mother ship into a bigger hull, refit your fighter to match, and send out remote outposts side-ships you can pilot yourself in their own hands-on minigames for extra materials.

Strip it to the bone.

ROLL THE ELEMENTS

Each round you throw your d12, and the face that lands on top goes into your stash. You build your d12 dice yourself before the run started.

THREE MAKE A STAR

Get three copies of the same creature in the same element and they fuse into one bigger, stronger unit. Do it again for 3 stars.

FILL THE BESTIARY

13 creature types, 13 elements, 3 stars each. The bestiary remembers every combination you have fielded, run after run.

BUILD ON TWO AXES

Every unit counts toward its type and its element at once. Put a third fire unit on the board and Fire 3 turns on for everyone.

WATCH IT PLAY OUT

Combat runs by itself and nobody leaves their hex. By the time the first skill goes off, your part is already done: you built the board.

BEAT THE BOSS, TAKE THE LOOT

Each stage ends in a boss fight. Win it and you pick one rare item out of three. One re-cuts a face on your die, another clones a unit onto your bench, a third pushes a creature up a star.

AWAKEN TO A WORLD THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN EMPTY.

You wake with no memory of how you arrived. Around you lies a frozen landscape, abandoned structures, and traces of something that went terribly wrong.

The deeper you explore, the more you realize that this place is not simply deserted.

Something is still here.

EMPTY LAND is a cinematic first-person survival horror experience focused on exploration, tension, environmental storytelling, puzzles, and terrifying encounters.

EXPLORE THE UNKNOWN

Search abandoned facilities, isolated structures, frozen paths, and forgotten locations as you piece together what happened. Every environment hides clues, secrets, and fragments of a much larger mystery.

SURVIVE THE NIGHTMARE

You are not the only one moving through the darkness. Stay alert, manage your surroundings, and survive encounters with threats that can appear when you least expect them.

SOLVE THE PUZZLES

Progress through dangerous environments by investigating your surroundings, finding useful items, unlocking secured areas, and solving environmental puzzles.

A CINEMATIC HORROR EXPERIENCE

Experience a realistic and atmospheric world built around darkness, isolation, environmental detail, fog, snow, sound, and carefully timed encounters.

KEY FEATURES

• First-person survival horror
• Atmospheric and realistic environments
• Exploration-driven gameplay
• Environmental puzzles and investigation
• Inventory and item management
• Story-rich mystery
• Cinematic presentation
• Tense enemy encounters
• Immersive environmental sound
• Single-player experience

HOW FAR WILL YOU GO?

The answers are waiting somewhere beyond the places you were never meant to find.

But remember—

The land may be empty.

You are not alone.

Out now in Early Access. 15 playable Kams, three of them new in the latest update: Toy Beyi, Kongıra and Od Kızı. More arrive in free updates.

Beat Kül-Kurgan in the free demo and Tunga, the Pioneer Kam, is waiting for you. Demo progress carries over (on the same PC).

about_html:
One person knows the way out. And they can't speak.

You're locked in a glass room facing a game-show stage. Next to you, your friends, in rooms exactly like yours. On stage, the MASTER — the only one who knows the way out — forbidden to say a word. They have mime and a giant board. Good luck.

A real escape room, in first person

Open drawers, flip the sofa cushions, spin the combination padlock, put the key in the door, the battery in the clock, the fuse in the fuse box and the bulb in the socket. Everything you find opens the next thing, until the front wall bursts open in confetti.
  • 12 hand-made rooms, 4 per difficulty. Easy: Grandma Zuzu's Parlour, Mr. Moustache's Barbershop, The Chef's Kitchen and The Treehouse. Medium: The Grand Hotel, The Night Sleeper, Channel 7 Studio and The Detective's Office. Advanced: The Bank Vault, The Old West Jail, The Inventor's Lab and Rádio Escape.
  • Identical rooms, on purpose: everyone plays the same room and the same hint is worth the same to all — nobody gets favoured.

With friends — 2 to 8

  • From 3 to 8 people, the show has its master: they take the stage and run the round with nothing but mime and drawings. Everyone gets a turn as master.
  • The tube: climb into the capsule, pick another contestant's room and get a few seconds to ruin their day. The brawl is the show.
  • The gas doesn't negotiate: when the clock runs out, it rises from the floor. You can make a run for it. Or faint beautifully, live on air.
  • Open voice inside your room, emotes and a hand slate to talk to your neighbour through the glass, and a phone that calls any room on speaker. The master never says a word.
  • With 8 people the show plays in duos: two people in the same room, one team.
  • Just the two of you? DUEL: the same rooms, one against the other, every hint on the giant board and open voice between you.

No friends online right now? Free Escape

  • Solo, on Easy, Medium or Advanced: one room at a time, one goal — escape before the gas. The big board shows the hint for the task at hand.
  • Rehearsal: a guided tutorial of about three minutes in The Dressing Room.

12 automata with screen faces and dozens of accessories, hundreds of thousands of outfit combinations, a 50-level career in the show and 18 achievements. 13 languages — the game opens in your Steam language.

Escape first. Sabotage the neighbors.

Hide more than your identity. Hide your body.

ESCAPE: FALSE COLORS is a multiplayer party game blending freeform painting, hidden identities, and parkour chases. Play with 2–6 players online, with bots available to fill empty slots, in a chaotic mix of suspense, light horror, and laughs.

Paint your disguise. Blend into your surroundings.
Paint freely on your body, using colors and patterns to match the environment and fool other players. That barely noticeable figure by the wall might be the very person you’re looking for.

Random roles. A killer among you.
Each round, play as the Sheriff, Murderer, or an Innocent. The Murderer hides their identity and waits for a chance to strike. The Sheriff must identify the killer, while the Innocents try to stay alive. Be careful who you trust.

Disguise blown? Run!
Jump, climb, and parkour through the map to lose your pursuer and find your next hiding spot.

If you enjoy MM2-style hidden-role gameplay, discover a new layer of body-paint camouflage and unpredictable parkour chases.

PAINT. LIE. RUN.

About This Game

"Same!" or "Wait, THAT'S your #1?!" — every answer is a good time.

A tier list party game where everyone ranks, and everyone guesses!

[ Simple Rules ]

Rank 5 words from S to D based on a prompt. That's it.

Take a prompt like "Best Hot Pot Ingredients."

There's no right answer — only YOUR ranking.

Even people who rarely play games can jump right in.

[ The Reveal Is Where It Gets Loud ]

One player is the star. Everyone else guesses how the star ranked the words.

A perfect match gets cheers. A wild miss gets big laughs.

Discover your friends' surprising tastes, the "I knew it!" moments, and who's really in sync.

At the end, awards like Ace Detective, Easiest to Read, Most Mysterious, and Contrarian

celebrate how well everyone read each other.

[ Two Ways to Play ]

■ Guess the Order

Guess the order the star ranked in secret.

■ All in Sync

Rank the players' own names — can everyone land on the exact same order?

See how many rounds in a row you can stay in sync.

[ 500+ Prompts ]

Over 500 prompts are included.

Make your own prompts and words, so inside jokes work too.

Publish your prompts to the Steam Workshop, and play prompts made by others.

Everyone's My Topics get mixed together, so the prompts your friends bring show up too.

[ Made for Streaming ]

In Streamer mode, you rank in a separate window that stays off stream. No spoilers.

Show your Room ID on stream and anyone can join, even if they're not on your friends list.

Viewer participation made easy.

Keep the streamer as the star and see who tops the "Streamer Sync Ranking."

[ Players ]

2–10 players

*Online only via Steam lobbies. Cannot be played solo.

(Streaming, videos, and monetization are welcome. No permission needed)

A town swallowed by a sinister cult. A veteran Exorcist Agent gone silent.

Now, a rookie Paranormal Investigator and her partner—the Ghost Hunting Hound—follow the traces he left behind, guided by a radio Handler, stepping into a dark and melancholy tragedy...

Exploration ADV & Stylish ACT

Welcome to the haunted town.

You can explore while being scared by paranormal phenomena.

Or, dash through bravely and scare the ghosts.

Creaking floors, flickering lights, ringing phones, brutal jump scares...

Whether you stop to watch the hauntings or ignore them and go take down the ghost, it’s all up to your playstyle.

Death Foresight & Instant Rewind

Touch the entrance door, and your extrasensory perception activates.

Dying inside means nothing—just a tragedy you foresaw before stepping through.

Instantly rewind to the front door, and break that death flag with a flawless run.

Ghost Hunting Hound & Buddy Action

Issue commands to your canine companion with intuitive controls.

Bark to draw enemy attention, or track scents to uncover hidden mechanisms.

And of course, don’t forget to give them a good pat when things go well!

Gunplay & Environmental Interaction

Tricky ghosts stand in your way—dodging bullets, raising shields, or possessing shadows or nearby objects.

To drive them back, you’ll need more than just gunfire—make full use of every object around you.

Hide & Sensory Boost

Every time you burst from cover, your sharpened extrasensory perception slows the world to a crawl.

Outrun every fear, and clear the haunted house.

(Too fast to control? Cool down—or git gud.)

EAR WE GO is a chaotic cooperative restaurant game where keeping the order chain running is the key to survival.

A waiter takes the customer's order and passes it to the self-service cashier. The cashier communicates it to the chef, who prepares the meal and sends it back to the waiter. One tiny mistake anywhere in the chain can throw the entire restaurant into chaos. If you can't get the food out in time, your restaurant goes under and the game is over.

Every run can play differently. Card choices change the way your restaurant works and alter the dynamics of the game, creating new challenges and experiences with every save. A clever choice can make your job easier, while the wrong one can turn a manageable shift into complete chaos.

Play with 1-6 players, coordinate with your team, and keep the restaurant alive. But communication isn't always easy: characters can only communicate with each other in certain areas, making positioning and coordination just as important as preparing the food.

Play solo or team up with up to 5 friends.Communication depends on your role: the waiter, cashier, and chef can hear specific teammates, but cannot communicate freely with everyone. Relay orders, coordinate your actions, prepare meals, and survive the rush together!

About the Game

Echo Doodle is a fast-paced, hand-drawn 2D action roguelite that takes place on the pages of a notebook.

Fight your way through doodled enemies and clear each stage. After every battle, choose new abilities and upgrades, combining effects that work together to create a different build each run.

You may start with nothing more than simple attacks and movement, but as your abilities pile up, the way you fight can change dramatically.

Create Your Own Build

What you choose—and how you upgrade it—is up to you.

Leave attacks behind as you dash through enemies, strengthen your shockwaves to sweep them away, stay airborne and prepare devastating downward strikes, or keep upgrading your basic attack until a simple slash becomes your strongest weapon.

Abilities can interact with different upgrades in different ways. Focus everything on a single ability, or combine multiple mechanics to create a playstyle of your own.

Every choice you make shapes how the rest of your run plays out.

Move Fast. Fight. Dodge.

Combat in Echo Doodle is built around fast movement and aggressive action.

Dodge incoming attacks, look for openings, and use jumps and dashes to move quickly across the battlefield. Fight on the ground or in the air, and make full use of the abilities you've collected as increasingly dangerous enemies stand in your way.

As you progress through the stages, new threats emerge—and powerful bosses await.

A Battle on a Notebook Page

The world of Echo Doodle isn't some grand fantasy kingdom.

It's a notebook.

A blue doodle character runs across lined paper, fighting enemies drawn in red. Attacks, shockwaves, and even enemy warning indicators are designed to look like they were scribbled directly onto the page.

Rather than a perfectly polished world, Echo Doodle aims to capture the feeling of doodles in the corner of a notebook suddenly coming to life.

How Far Can You Go?

Clear stages, choose your abilities, and build something powerful.

Maybe this run you'll push your dash to its absolute limit.
Maybe next time you'll build around staying in the air.
Or maybe that ordinary basic attack will become the strongest weapon you have.

Turn the page and see what awaits.

The world is ending. It has done so before.

In Echo Harvest, survival is not about saving a single life. It is about building something that can endure across timelines.

Establish settlements, gather resources, explore an increasingly dangerous world and prepare your colonies against corrupted creatures. Your settlements develop autonomously, constructing buildings and defences using the resources you provide.

Beyond the safety of the Home Flame, corruption steadily closes in. You cannot stop time. You can only decide what to accomplish before it runs out.

Your past lives become your workforce.

What you do during each life determines the Echo you leave behind. Gathering, building, exploring, defending, transporting supplies and harvesting resources contribute towards different Echo specialisations. The life you lead shapes the Echo that follows you into the future.

Over time, a lone Keeper becomes the centre of a growing network of settlements populated by the remnants of lives that came before.

Every timeline is a race against collapse.

Supply your settlements with resources as they autonomously develop farms, housing, storage, walls and defensive turrets. Establish new colonies. Discover forgotten places and valuable resources. Strengthen your settlements while balancing expansion against the growing threat they attract.

Echo Dust can help stabilise a failing timeline, but it is limited. Eventually you must decide whether you are ready to construct a Beacon and Ascend — sacrificing the present to strengthen what comes next.

Fail, and the timeline is lost.

Ascend, and the struggle begins again under greater pressure.

But history remembers either way.

Echo Harvest records the story of your timeline as you play. Important discoveries, settlements, battles, losses, periods of prosperity and moments of collapse become part of an illustrated Chronicle of that world.

When a timeline finally ends in victory or total loss, its Chronicle is published to your Timeline Library and can be exported as an illustrated PDF — a permanent history of a world that no longer exists.

Shape the Past. Save the Future.

about_html:
TO SEE, YOU MUST SPEAK. TO SPEAK IS TO BE FOUND.

There is no light down there. Every sound sends out a wave that tears the world out of the dark for a second, then lets it go. Your voice is your flashlight. It is also your trail.

EVERYTHING DOWN THERE HEARS YOU

A whisper lights a couple of metres. A scream lights half the floor, and everything hunting down there hears it too. Footsteps, a dropped crate, a slammed door: there is no harmless noise. But noise is also bait. Throw something into the dark and watch what comes for it.

TAKE THE JOB. BRING IT BACK.

Pick a contract, ride the lift down, get the job done before the shift ends. Haul out what you came for, even if it is the last crew, and load it on the truck. Every descent is a new level. The deeper you go, the better the pay and the worse your odds. Whatever you fail to bring back is gone.

TRUST YOUR EARS. NOT YOUR CREW.

Some doors open only when you sing the right note. One creature speaks in your teammate's voice. Another makes you see a monster where your friend is standing, and you will swing first. 1–4 players.

WHAT YOU NEED

A microphone, required: it is not voice chat, it is the core mechanic. Headphones, required: the audio is positional, and speakers will give you away with your own voice.

Earth needs antibodies. You are one of them.

The Clamor came down from the sky and took the towns. Their bodies were never built for this world, and you carry the one thing they cannot survive: a virus.

Infect alien hosts by night. Engineer new strains by day. Stay ahead of vaccines, quarantine efforts, and increasingly dangerous enemies as you fight your way from isolated villages to the Clamor mothership.

Your weapon is a disease

One bite seeds an outbreak.

Design your virus by balancing transmission, symptoms, and lethality. Spread it through contact, contamination, or the air itself. Delay symptoms to reach critical mass. Increase lethality to thin enemy ranks. Adapt your strategy as the Clamor develops new countermeasures.

The outbreak spreads without you

Every infected host becomes a carrier. Diseases spread through the population while you hide, mutate your strain, and prepare for the next night. Multiple outbreaks can exist at once, creating a web of infections that evolves across the entire campaign.

Hunt by echolocation

You are a bat, and you see the world through sound.

Your chirps sketch the environment into existence before it fades back into darkness. Scan pulses reveal infection status in the only color the world allows itself. Every night becomes a balance between information and exposure.

Sound helps you see. Sound also gives away your position.

Stay hidden in vents, rafters, and dark corners while you search for new hosts. If the Clamor spots you, patrols respond. Soldiers mobilize. Cybernetic hounds begin the hunt.

A world that fights back

The Clamor learns from every outbreak. Return to a town and you may find quarantine zones, medical facilities, armed patrols, and new defenses. The more successful your diseases become, the harder the enemy works to stop them.

Mutate faster than they can adapt — or watch your pandemic die.

A handmade visual language

Every frame is rendered as ink and pencil on paper. The world exists as the bat perceives it: incomplete, temporary, and shaped by sound itself. When the world fills in around you, a sound wave has landed. When you see color, something is infected.

The hunt starts at dusk. - Wishlist now.

Descend into a world built to challenge you. We fused elements of turn-based RPGs with the mechanics and balance of competitive card games. Learn from every defeat, push deeper, and prove your strategy against other Seekers fighting their way to the top.

  • Deep Turn-Based Tactics: Every move matters. Summon your Eidolons, plan many moves ahead, manage cooldowns and resources, and never underestimate the enemy—they know what they're doing. Brute force will only take you so far—the deeper you go, the more the game demands that you understand and exploit its mechanics.

  • Learn, Adapt, Overcome: The game isn't designed to let you win every fight on your first attempt. Study your enemies, recognize their patterns and weaknesses, rethink your build, and return with a better answer. Knowledge is as much a part of your arsenal as the tools you bring into battle.

  • Race against Other Seekers: You may fight alone, but you are never alone in the challenge. Other players are making their way through the same world, facing the same dangers and searching for strategies that can take them further. Push your build to its limits and fight your way up the rankings.

  • Put Your Skill to the Test: If monsters aren’t enough of a challenge, take on real players. Bring your best build and strategy into PvP and find out how you hold up when there’s a Seeker on the other side.

Echoe of Memory: AI Profiler is a near-future mystery detective adventure in which you reinvestigate cold cases from the past together with your AI partner, ECHO.

You play as Makoto Kuroiwa, an investigator assigned to the Cold Case Investigation Support Office. By examining crime scene photos, surveillance footage, public social media posts, police databases, and records related to the people involved, you search for the contradictions left behind in each case.

AI is not there to simply give you the answer. Using the analysis candidates presented by ECHO as clues, it is up to you to decide what should be treated as evidence and which information should be questioned.

The first case is “The Ichijo Family Heiress Kidnapping Case,” in which the daughter of a prestigious family vanished from a study. A ransacked room. Muddy footprints. A suspicious figure captured on surveillance footage. Every record seems to point to a kidnapping. But the more you reconnect the evidence, the more small discrepancies begin to emerge in the official explanation.

Organize suspects, related parties, and evidence through a relationship chart. Investigate suspicious areas in crime scene images. Select key information from social media and database records. Finally, submit your final report based on “WHO / WHEN / WHERE / WHAT / HOW / WHY.”

This is a story about uncovering the “echoes of memory” buried within old case files.
The truth lies within the records. But to reach it, you will need your own deduction.

Features

  • A near-future mystery adventure guided by your AI partner, ECHO

  • A suspense story themed around unsolved cases, cold cases, and criminal investigations

  • An investigation system that spans crime scene photos, social media, police databases, and surveillance footage

  • Relationship chart analysis that visualizes the links between people, evidence, and incidents

  • A final report system where you organize gathered information into the 5W1H to reconstruct the truth

  • A visual novel-style story combined with evidence-selection deduction gameplay

Master a Massive Collection

Dive into a deep, tactile first-person simulation where your organizational skills are put to the ultimate test.

  • 3,600 Cards: Sort, stack, and display a staggering variety of trading cards.

  • Elemental Themes: Categorize your inventory across ten distinct elemental types, from Fire and Water to Void and Toxin.

  • Perfect Placement: Find the exact right shelf for every monster based on its element and level.

Two Levels to Organize

Bring order to the cozy card shop, then step into the brand-new Level 2: a sprawling glass greenhouse buried under a fresh mountain of cards.

  • The HoloPodium: Hold any card near the HoloPodium and it projects that monster's entire evolution line, from Level 1 to Level 3, so you always know which cards belong together.

  • Full Family Sets: In the greenhouse, every cabinet holds one complete evolution family across its three shelves. Place the first card and the cabinet locks to that family with a glowing holographic label, so only its evolutions can join it.

Unlock Magical Abilities

Sorting thousands of cards by hand is tough, but you have a few tricks up your sleeve! Earn Skill Points (SP) for correct placements and upgrade your character in a fully unrestricted Skill Tree.

Build Your Cozy Haven

  • First-Person Immersion: Experience the tactile joy of picking up, inspecting, and placing every single card in a fully 3D environment.

  • Set the Vibe: Walk over to the shop's jukebox and blast an energetic soundtrack—featuring lo-fi tracks keep your sorting rhythm going.

Ready to organize the chaos? Grab your first card and start shelving!

The Nightmare is Online.
You are Levi, trapped inside a mission you were designated to by the ECHO Program, a secret government investigation team, with something that was never meant to wake up. Echoes in Static is a tense, psychological survival horror experience where every footstep matters and every shadow hides a threat. You were trained for days like these, but are you trained for what each environment has to offer you? we will see ECHO.

You are being hunted by the EX Program, custom built, rogue animatronics driven by a terrifyingly cold, calculating logic. They do not feel pity. They do not tire and they know exactly where you are.

Will you scavenge each facility to uncover the horrifying truth and find a way out with each area explored? Or will you build the tools necessary to take the fight to the enemy? The choice is yours.


With exploring the outbreak that was caused by the EX Program around the whole country of the USA you will uncover multiple different things throughout your journey and also come across new play strategies and completely different areas you will have to adapt to throughout your way through the ruins of the company called Static Electronics, Static Electronics made the EX Program but something about there AI Went wrong.


Will you ECHO uncover the truth behind the country wide Statonic Outbreak and shut this nightmare down forever? or will you be another Echo In Static.

Unleash the Storm. Survive the Night.

Echoes of Aethelgard is a fast-paced, horde-survival roguelite where you are the bullet hell. Step into a cursed valley, face endless waves of monsters, and build an arsenal capable of shattering reality itself.

Will you cleanse the corruption, or be swallowed by the Void? (Spoiler: The Void has a very high appetite.)

Evolve Your Arsenal

Start with a single blade and build your way to godhood. Every weapon features a distinct upgrade path culminating in devastating Ultimate Abilities.

  • Celestial Rain: Transform a simple bow into a localized orbital strike that shields you while erasing your enemies from the map.

  • Earthshatter Maul: Upgrade a heavy hammer into an earthen nova machine that stuns everything on screen—and probably shakes your desk in real life.

  • The Secret Stash: Unlock powerful, hidden weapons that turn the "survival" part of the game into a "clean-up crew" simulation.

Synergize and Survive

  • Keep the Combo Alive: Chain kills to ignite your combo meter. Higher combos mean massive buffs and faster clearing. It’s like a rhythm game, but with more skeletons.

  • Meta-Progression: Collect shards and coins. Spend shards in the Armory for permanent stat boosts, or gamble your coins on powerful, run-specific Temp Buffs.

  • The Jackpot: Fill your meter to trigger a moment of pure invincibility. It’s the perfect tool for breaking out of a tight corner or just being a menace for 10 seconds.

Cinematic Lore & Epic Bosses

Uncover the tragic history of Aethelgard through beautifully illustrated story sequences. Just don't get too distracted by the lore, or the Liche Lord, the Wasteland Beast, or the Void Corruptor will turn you into a footnote in history.

Learn their patterns, dodge the chaos, and claim the rewards they were definitely not using anyway.

A story-driven 2.5D turn-based RPG where the journeys of two parties unfold through alternating perspectives.

　

Two Journeys, Guided by Fire

In a world where the cycle of souls exists, "Flame Wardens" are sworn to protect it.

Haku, a Flame Warden from a town at the western edge, journeys toward the heart of the land—the sacred peak of Coral—to fulfill his duty, joined by his demi-human best friend Kaji and Mikoto, an enigmatic former mafia member.

From a town at the eastern edge, Ren, another Flame Warden, sets out for the sacred peak of Coral, joined by his childhood friend Maruka and a mysterious elder named Rakan.

Two journeys, unfolding through alternating perspectives. What awaits them at journey’s end?

Unlock Hidden Truths with "Key Words"

Discover "Key Words" throughout your journey. Present them to the right people to unlock the world's hidden lore. Which words will you choose—and to whom? Rely on your intuition and reasoning to piece together the story.

Strategic Combat Shaped by Flexible Builds and "Shields"

A turn-based command battle system enhanced with unique strategic elements. No random encounters—every battle is a carefully crafted tactical challenge.

  • "Shields" That Dictate the Flow of Battle: Every combatant has a "Shield" that reduces incoming HP damage. At the start of battle, focus on wearing down enemy shields, then shift to damaging HP as the situation evolves. The choice—wear down their shields or strike at their HP—can turn the tide of battle.

  • Flexible Ability Builds: Traditional leveling has been replaced with a system where you allocate "Combat Points" earned through story progression. Customize your characters by assigning Combat Points to active skills, passive abilities, and stat boosts to suit your strategy.

  • Status Effects and Gear Customization: When enabled by gear, status buildup accumulates with each attack, eventually triggering status effects in a Soulslike-inspired system. It can become a powerful advantage even against formidable foes. Slot "Spirit Stones" into your weapons and armor to create highly personalized gear—such as builds focused on shield-breaking or inflicting status effects.

(An "Easy Mode" is also planned for players who prefer to focus on the story and exploration.)

 　

Estimated Playtime: 10–20 hours (may vary depending on playstyle and exploration)

◆ Story

"It's just a replica — but I loved it more than the real thing."

Rei Shiotani is a high school boy who loves replica guns more than anything.

Law-abiding — exemplary — unremarkable —

Then, a turning point arrives.

"You've got a good eye, Rei. No doubt about it."

Standing there was Kotaro — a huge man with an oblivious look on his face.

A salesman's smile, and a scout's gaze...

"A friend of mine runs a business. Want to try working part-time there?"

The flattery was excessive, and deep down Rei didn't trust it — but he had no choice but to jump at the offer.

Someone had recognized his talent. That alone was enough.

What lies ahead — a summer vacation of just fifteen days.

What will Rei see — and what will he choose not to see?
